text: Start the chapter by showing a glass of water and asking students where it came from before it reached the tap.
💧 **Have you ever wondered** where the water in your tap comes from? Does it magically appear out of nowhere?
🤔 **Socratic Question:** If you leave a bucket outside in the rain, it fills up. But where does the river get its water when it's not raining?

content.title: The Journey of Water
content.description: Water comes from rain, fills rivers and lakes, and even hides under the ground.

text: 📖 **The Reveal:** These places are called **Sources of Water**. The main source of all water on Earth is rain. Other sources are rivers, lakes, ponds, and wells.

definition: The place where something begins or comes from.

question: Which of these is the main source of water on Earth?

text: 🪞 **Reflection:** Think about your own house. Do you get water from a well, a river, or a tap connected to a large overhead tank?
🌍 **Connection:** Just like a mobile phone needs a charger to work, humans, animals, and plants need these water sources to survive and grow!

title: Water Artist
description: Draw a beautiful picture of a river flowing from the tall mountains all the way to the deep blue sea.

text: Students often think all water on Earth is drinkable. Emphasize that ocean water is salty and not fit for drinking.
🧊 **Have you noticed** that an ice cube disappears when left in the hot sun? Where does it go?
🤔 **Socratic Question:** If you boil water on a stove, you see white steam rising. Is that steam also made of water?

content.title: Forms of Water
content.description: Water can change its shape! It can be hard like a rock, flow like a river, or fly like a cloud.

text: 📖 **The Reveal:** Water is magical! It exists in three forms: **Solid** (Ice), **Liquid** (Water), and **Gas** (Water Vapor or Steam).

definition: The gas form of water, created when water is heated.

question: What is the solid form of water called?

text: 🪞 **Reflection:** Next time you have a cold drink, touch the ice cube and remember you are holding solid water!
🌍 **Connection:** The fluffy white clouds you see in the sky are made of tiny water drops and water vapor. That's how we get rain!

title: Ice Magic
description: Put a small cup of water in the freezer at night. Check it the next morning and see how liquid turns into solid!

text: 🚰 **Imagine** waking up one day and there is not a single drop of water in your house. What would you do?
🤔 **Socratic Question:** Our Earth is mostly covered with blue ocean water, but we can't drink it because it's too salty. So, do we really have endless water to drink?

content.title: Save Every Drop
content.description: Only a tiny bit of water on Earth is fresh and safe for us to drink. Every drop is precious.

text: 📖 **The Reveal:** Since drinkable water is very limited, we must practice **Water Conservation**, which means saving water and never wasting it.

definition: The careful use and protection of something, like water, so it does not run out.

question: Which of the following is a good habit for saving water?
options: Leaving the tap open while brushing teeth
Using a bucket to take a bath instead of a shower
Throwing away leftover water from your water bottle
Playing with the garden hose pipe

text: 🪞 **Reflection:** Think about today. Did you see any water being wasted? How could you have stopped it?
🌍 **Connection:** Saving water means saving life on Earth. Without water, there would be no plants, no animals, and no us. We are all connected by water.

title: Water Detective
description: Become a Water Detective! Find one leaking tap in your home or school and ask an adult to help fix it.
